![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14264040/assets/8927e58849984fbb42a7a3856e3b3509b9729b65031e066d29c6f94747ee5b6b.png)

Points $C$ and $D$ are shown in the picture above. Find $|\overset{\to }{CD}|.$
question.worked_solution:
From the picture, we obtain $C(-3,4)$ and $D(2,3).$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned} & \overset{\to }{OC}=c=-3i+4j, \\  & \overset{\to }{OD}=d=2i+3j.\end{aligned}
$$

Expressing $\overset{\to }{CD}$ as the difference of position vectors, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{CD} & =\overset{\to }{OD}-\overset{\to }{OC} \\  & =d-c \\  & =(2i+3j)-(-3i+4j) \\  & =5i-j\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the formula for the magnitude of a vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|\overset{\to }{CD}| & =\sqrt{{5}^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{25+1} \\  & =\sqrt{26}.\end{aligned}
$$
